$comment: Midori — HTML markup inside JS/TS template literals.
The TypeScript grammar gives a template literal body a single contentName,
'string.template.ts', and only two sub-patterns: ${...} and character
escapes. So `<div class="muted">` is one scope from end to end, and no
theme can split it — tags, attribute names and values are all one colour.
This injection emits the scopes the theme already styles for real .html
new palette values are introduced; the existing tag/attribute rules just
start firing where they previously could not.
The selector subtracts meta.template.expression because ${...} inherits
string.template from the enclosing literal — without it these rules would
also fire on real code inside interpolations.

$comment-interpolation: Included first everywhere, so ${...} keeps its normal expression
highlighting inside a tag and inside an attribute value. Without this
the injection's span would shadow the base grammar's substitution rule.
$comment-attribute-value: Quoted values are matched explicitly rather than left to fall through.
That protects their contents from the attribute-name rule (a value like
"a=b" would otherwise pick up a false attribute) and lands them on
string.quoted, which is the colour they already had.
